en.headline: Beauty and fitness trades back seven-day cooling-off, Yau says
en.dek: The commerce chief told RTHK the government hopes to put an amendment to the Trade Descriptions Ordinance before the Legislative Council in the first half of next year.
body: Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau said on Saturday that beauty parlours and fitness operators had voiced strong support for a statutory seven-day cooling-off period on prepaid service contracts, after a two-month public consultation on amending the Trade Descriptions Ordinance.

Speaking on RTHK’s Saturday Accountability programme, Yau said the industries also regarded seven days as sufficient, noting that the period follows practice in a number of other economies and was considered workable. He said the consultation had drawn a range of views from both operators and the public.

On the contract-value threshold that would trigger the cooling-off rule, Yau said the two trades held different views because typical contract amounts differ widely. He said the government would seek a balance that protects consumers while taking account of operators’ difficulties.

Yau said that once the administration had finished studying the responses, it hoped to submit a proposal to the Legislative Council in the first half of next year so that the amendment could be completed as soon as possible.

zh.headline: 丘應樺：美容健身業界支持7日冷靜期
zh.dek: 商經局局長在港台《星期六問責》表示，完成研究後希望明年上半年把修訂《商品說明條例》的方案提交立法會。
body: 商務及經濟發展局局長丘應樺周六表示，政府就美容及健身服務預繳式消費合約修訂《商品說明條例》、引入7日法定冷靜期的兩個月公眾諮詢已經完成，美容及健身業界均非常支持有關安排。
他在港台節目《星期六問責》稱，業界亦認為7日時間足夠，因為建議已參照不少其他國家及經濟體的慣例，認為可以執行。他指諮詢期間收到業界和市民的不同意見。
至於觸發冷靜期的合約金額門檻，丘應樺表示兩個行業看法不一，因為合約金額差異很大。他強調當局會保障消費者權益，同時照顧經營者的困難，以作出平衡。
他表示，完成研究後希望明年上半年把方案提交立法會，盡快完成修例。
